headline: Approved bus yard at 780 James P. Casey Rd. and two restaurants at 838 Farmington Avenue; recommended smoke and vape shop moratorium.
summary: Approved a site plan for a bus yard at 780 James P. Casey Rd. and a site plan for two take-out restaurants at 838 Farmington Avenue. Recommended positive referrals to the Zoning Commission on a smoke and vape shop moratorium and a rezoning of Lot 101 Terryville Avenue, and to the City Council on two Union Street lot sales. Continued a subdivision hearing for 107 Chestnut Street and scheduled a public hearing on a manufacturing facility at 190 Business Park Drive for September 28, 2026.

plain_text:
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
 
BRISTOL PLANNING COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
REGULAR MEETING OF MONDAY AUGUST 24, 2026 
 
CALL TO ORDER: 
 
By: Chairman Veits Time: 6:00 P.M. Place: City Hall 
   Council Chambers 
   111 North Main Street 
   First Floor 
 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS: Chairman William Veits (Chairman) X   
 John Soares (Vice Chairman) X  
 Jon Pose X  
 Tracey Bacchus  X 
 Christopher Nardi (Acting Secretary) X  
  X  
    
ALTERNATE MEMBERS: Kiana Small X  
 Greg Klimek X  
 DeWayne Wynn X  
    
STAFF: Robert M. Flanagan, AICP, City Planner X  
    
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Per the order of Chairman Veits the meeting was called to order at 6:00 P.M. 
Chairman Veits reminded the Commission the next Regular Meeting of the Planning Commission is Monday, 
September 28, 2026. 
 
2. Public Participation 
 
The Chairman read into the record the protocol for public participation to the public audience. Chairman Veits 
indicated the items subject to public participation would be Items 4.a. and 4.b., under Receipt of New Applications; 
Items 6.a., under Zoning Commission Referrals; Item 7.a and 7.b., under City Council and Other Referrals; and Item 
8.a. under New Business.  
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
 
a.  Regular Meeting — July 27, 2026 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, regular Commissioners Pose and Soares with alternate Commissioner Klimek and 
Wynn to vote on the July 27, 2026, regular minutes.  
 
MOTION : Move to approve the minutes of the July 27, 2026, reg ular meeting. 
 
By: Veits Seconded: Pose. 
 
For: Wynn, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 2 – 
 
 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Commissioner Alternate 
Commissioner Klimek as voting Commissioners this evening. The Chairman designated Commissioner Nardi as Acting 
Secretary this evening. 
 
4. Receipt of New Applications 
 
a. Application #454 — Site Plan for a Bus Yard at 780 James P. Casey Rd; Assessor's Map 65, Lot 3; IP-5 
(Industrial Park) zone; Dattco, Inc., applicant; 780 JPC Road Holdings, LLC, owner. 
 
MOTION: Move that Application #454 be placed under “New Business” on this Agenda. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Soares. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
b.  Application #455 — Site Plan for a 29,500 sq. ft. manufacturing facility at 190 Business Park Drive; 
Assessor's Map 3, Lot 6; IP-1 (Industrial Park) zone; Integrity Manufacturing, LLC, applicant; City of 
Bristol, owner. 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Commissioner Alternate 
Commissioner Klimek to vote on Application # 455. 
 
Charles Talmadge of Development Planning Solutions, 225 North Main Street, representing the applicant indicated 
the request was to construct a 30,000 sq. ft. manufacturing facility that does metal finishing and grinding. Mr. 
Talmadge said the applicant is requesting to locate into the industrial park. 
 
MOTION: Move that Application #455 be scheduled for a Public Hearing at the next Regular Meeting of the 
Planning Commission on September 28, 2026.  
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Soares. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
5 Public Hearings 
 
a.  Application #453 — Subdivision - 107 Chestnut Street (3 lots) Assessor’s Map 
29, Lot 253/30; RM-5 (Mixed Residential) zone; Chestnut and Locust Holdings, LLC, owner/applicant. 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on Application #453. 
 
Charles Talmadge of Development Planning Solutions, 225 North Main Street, representing the applicant, explained 
this was a corner lot on Chestnut Street and Locust Street that has a multi-family house on the property. Mr. 
Talmadge noted the request was for a subdivision to repurpose the vacant land that goes with this property for two 
additional house lots.  
 
The consultant reviewed comments received that included the shed would be removed.  Mr. Talmadge view was the 
proposal did not need open space because of the properties distance from the Rockwell Park. The consultant would 
continue to work on the comments with Staff as the comments are received. Mr. Talmadge noted the lots would be 
compliant for the RM-5 zone.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 3 – 
 
 
 
Staff would send a link for the Subdivision Regulations to update the Commissioners on subdivisions.  
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
Commission inquiries: The consultant indicated the total property was 2,000 sq. ft. Mr. Talmadge said there may be a 
maximum of 4 units because it was unsure if there would be single family houses or duplex units. The consultant 
specified there were no inland wetlands or aquifer protection areas on the property. If approved, Mr. Talmadge 
indicated the duplexes would be constructed side by side but there are topographic concerns.  
 
MOTION: Move to continue the Public Hearing on Application #453 to the next Regular Meeting of the Planning 
Commission on September 28, 2026. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Nardi. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
6. Zoning Commission Referrals 
 
a.  Application AZR 26-03 — Pursuant to Article IV, Section 17.1.4.C.1: Referral from the Zoning Commission of 
proposed amendments to the Zoning Regulations to add: 1. Article IV, Section 17.3: Moratoria; 2. Article IV, 
Section 17.3.1: Authority and Procedures; 3. Article IV, Section 17.3.2: Moratorium on the Establishment or 
Expansion of Smoke and Vape Shops in all zones. Initiated by: Bristol Zoning Commission. 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on Application AZR 26-03. 
 
The City Planner explained the referral was initiated by the Zoning Commission that had a meeting on August 20, 
2026. Staff reviewed the details of the PowerPoint presentation that was presented by the IMEG consultant at the 
August 20, 2026, Zoning Commission meeting to explain the referral to the Commission.  
 
The City Planner overviewed the presentation statistics of the increase in health concerns of younger people and the 
CDC’s recommendation to reduce smoke and vape shops. Staff stated from the report the total numbers of 44 
existing businesses, 32 active businesses and 51 inactive businesses. The City Planner went over the C.G.S. 
definitions of the dealers’ licenses to sell the electronic devices and the definitions of tobacco products.  
 
Staff said for a moratoria to be added the Regulations, a definition of a smoke and vape shop was required and a 
draft definition was provided. The City Planner indicated municipalities had authority to regulate or prohibit specific 
commercial uses under the C.G.S. 8-2. The Zoning Regulations are specifically designed to “promote health and 
general public welfare.”  
 
Staff indicated the Zoning Commission accepted the application at their meeting on Thursday August 20, 2026. The 
City Planner noted the Zoning Commission would have a public hearing on Application AZR 26-03 at their September 
meeting. Staff stated the Planning Commission can vote on the Zoning Commission Referral this evening.  
 
The City Planner read into the record the new Moratorium Regulation that was proposed to be added the Zoning 
Regulation, under Sections 17.3. Staff read into the record the new proposed Moratorium on Smoke and Vape Shops, 
under Section 17.3.2.  
 
Commissioner Klimek understood the concerns but was more concerned the City may end up in a lawsuit over this 
matter.  
 
MOTION : Motion to send a positive referral to the Zoning Commi ssion.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 4 – 
 
 
 
The Planning Commission finds that the Zoning referral, as presented, is generally consistent with the goals and 
policies of the 2015 Plan of Conservation and Development (POCD), amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
By: Nardi Seconded: Soares. 
Roll Call Vote:  
Soares: yes. 
Pose: yes. 
Nardi: yes.  
Klimek: no. 
Veits: yes. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The Application #AZR 26-03 is recommended for a positive referral.  
 
Item #6.b., under Zoning Commission Referrals, Application #2571, was added to the agenda. 
 
b.  Application #2571 — Change of Zone from R-40 (Single-Family Residential) zone to I (General 
Industrial) zone at Lot 101 Terryville Avenue; Assessor's Map 61, Lots 101; Industrial Industries LLC, 
applicant/owner. 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on Application #2571. 
 
The City Planner said this was a referral from the Zoning Commission to the Planning Commission. Staff noted the 
applicant owns the property and wants to change the zone for an industrial use.  
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Ave., representing the applicant, explained the residential zone area on the site 
does not have any frontage. Attorney Ziogas noted the applicant owned the 7.4-acre property (I-Zone.) The attorney 
added the applicant purchased a 2.15-acre residential site from St. Joseph’s Church. Attorney Ziogas stated the 
property is surrounded by industrial zone property except for the property near the St. Joseph Church. The attorney 
verified the residential zone property does not have frontage or any access. 
 
Attorney Ziogas pointed out the steep contours from 500 to 460 with a 40 ft. elevation on the property. The attorney 
highlighted the industrial zoned properties are important because there were few industrial zoned properties. 
Attorney Ziogas claimed the residential zone property had no use in this area. The attorney requested a positive 
referral be sent to the Zoning Commission.  
 
MOTION : Motion to send a positive referral to the Zoning Commi ssion.  
 
The Planning Commission finds that the Zoning referral, as presented, is generally consistent  with the goals and 
policies of the 2015 Plan of Conservation and Development (POCD), amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
By: Nardi Seconded: Klimek. 
 
MOTION : Motion to send a positive referral to the Zoning Commi ssion. 
 
The Planning Commission finds that the Zoning referral, as presented, is generally consistent  with the goals and 
policies of the 2015 Plan of Conservation and Development (POCD), amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
For: Nardi, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: Klimek. 
Abstain: None.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 5 – 
 
 
The Application #2571 is recommended for a positive referral.  
 
7.  City Council and Other Referrals 
 
a. C.G.S. 8-24 Referral: 
Union Street — Map 31, Lot 4 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on C.G.S. 8-24 Referral, Union Street — Map 31, Lot 4. 
 
Staff indicated this referral is from the City Council of excess land that the City would like to sell. This is a vacant lot 
but a referral was needed from the Planning Commission. The maps for the application were reveiwed.  
 
Staff read into the record the e-mail dated August 6, 2026, from Attorney Jeffrey Steeg, Office of Corporation 
Counsel, regarding Lot 4, Union Street & Lot 6 (formerly 164 Union Street.) 
 
Commission inquiries: The City Planner noted there was no interest from any City departments for any use of the 
property.  
 
MOTION : Move to send a positive referral to the City Council for the C.G.S. 8-24 referral for: Union Street — Map 
31, Lot 4. 
 
The Planning Commission finds that the C.G.S. 8-24 referral for the City of Bristol to sell the property on Union 
Street, Map 31, Lot 4, is generally consistent with the goals and policies of the 2015 Plan of Conservation and 
Development (POCD), amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
By: Nardi Seconded: Klimek. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The CT General Statute 8-24 Referral is recommended for approval. 
 
b.  C.G.S. 8-24 Referral: 
164 Union Street — Map 31, Lot 6 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on C.G.S. 8-24 Referral, 164 Union Street — Map 31, Lot 6. 
 
MOTION : Motion to send a positive referral to the City Council  for the C.G.S. 8-24 referral for: 164 Union Street, 
Map 31, Lot 6. 
 
The Planning Commission finds that the C.G.S. 8-24 referral for the City of Bristol to sell the property, is generally 
consistent with the goals and policies of the 2015 Plan of Conservation and Development (POCD), amended to April 
1, 2018. 
 
By: Nardi Seconded:. Klimek. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The CT General Statute 8-24 Referral is recommended for approval.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 6 – 
 
 
 
8.  New Business 
 
a.  Application #452 — Site Plan for Two (2) Take-Out Restaurants at 838 Farmington Avenue; Assessor's Map 
48, Lot 182; BG (General Business) zone; Anand Jaiswal, applicant / Vernon Properties, owner. 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on Application #452. 
 
Staff reviewed the original proposed plans were for 3 restaurants but the plans were redesigned for 2 restaurants. 
Staff reported that the applicant responded to the comments. It was noted that the original plan had an addition with 
and did not have traffic circulating around the building; the plans were revised to add parking and keep the traffic 
pattern the same. The applicant received approval from the Aquifer Protection Area Agency that is an unregulated 
activity. It was noted that there were only a few outstanding comments.  
 
Anand Jaiswal, 31 Florence Way, Farmington, representing the applicant, explained the two restaurants proposed are 
Cold Stone Creamery and Wetzel’s Pretzels. Mr. Jaiswal added that the building addition was unfeasible for him 
because the addition would be $125,000 because the roof would have to be reconstructed. 
 
Commission inquiries: Mr. Jaiswal stated there was no watercourses near the property.  
 
MOTION: Move to approve Application #452 — Site Plan for Two (2) Take-Out Restaurants at 838 Farmington 
Avenue; Assessor's Map 48, Lot 182; BG (General Business) zone; Anand Jaiswal, applicant / Vernon 
Properties, owner, with the following stipulations: 
 
1.  The Plan shall not be signed off until all remaining staff comments have been addressed and the plan revised 
accordingly. 
 
2.  All site improvements which have not been satisfactorily completed by the time a Certificate of Occupancy is 
applied for shall be bonded in accordance with Article 4 Section 16.3.16. of the Zoning Regulations. The 
performance bond shall be posted by the applicant with the City before the Certificate of Occupancy being 
issued. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Soares. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
 
Item #4, Receipt of New Applications, Application #454 was resumed at this time. 
 
b.  Application #454 — Site Plan for a Bus Yard at 780 James P. Casey Rd; Assessor's Map 65, Lot 3; IP-5 
(Industrial Park) zone; Dattco, Inc., applicant; 780 JPC Road Holdings, LLC, owner 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on Application #454. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, reminded the Commission an approval was 
received from the Commission for a text amendment for the applicant a few months ago to allow a bus yard in the 
IP-5 Zone that was extended from the original I-Zone to the IP-5 Zone.  
 
Attorney Ziogas noted Dattco, Inc. is the applicant for the property to park 120 school buses with 150 employees. 
The attorney indicated industrial zone properties are difficult to obtain but the applicant was looking to purchase a 
suitable site. Attorney Ziogas said the applicant has a 1-year lease with 2 one-year options until there is a permanent 
location. The attorney indicated on site there would be the school buses and a small office with rest rooms. Attorney
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 7 – 
 
 
Ziogas specified the business hours of Monday to Friday 6:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. The attorney added that athletic 
events would require later hours and Saturdays. 
 
Attorney Ziogas pointed out this was the old New Departure site so there has been in the past a significant amount 
of parking and traffic. The attorney reviewed the existing building uses on the site. Attorney Ziogas noted a traffic 
report was included with the application that concluded the existing and proposed traffic would be less intense than 
the prior New Departure. Attorney Ziogas described the above ground fuel storage that would be on the site. The 
attorney indicated the existing lighting would be used for the plan. 
Staff inquiries: The attorney indicated the location was temporary for now. Attorney Ziogas said a zone change may 
be requested for parcels in the future by the applicant. 
 
MOTION: Move to move to approve Application #454 — Site Plan for a Bus Yard at 780 James P. Casey Rd; 
Assessor's Map 65, Lot 3; IP-5 (Industrial Park) zone; Dattco, Inc., applicant; 780 JPC Road Holdings, 
LLC, owner. 
 
1.  The Plan shall not be signed off until all remaining staff comments have been addressed and the plan revised 
accordingly. 
 
2.  All site improvements which have not been satisfactorily completed by the time a Certificate of Completion is 
applied for shall be bonded in accordance with Article 4 Section 16.3.16. of the Zoning Regulations. The 
performance bond shall be posted by the applicant with the City before the Certificate of Completion  being 
issued. 
 
By: Nardi Seconded: Klimek. 
 
For: Nardi, Klimek, Pose, Soares and Veits. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
9.  Old Business 
The was no old business.  
 
10.  Staff Reports 
a. 2028 Bristol Plan of Conservation and Development 
 
Staff updated the Commission on the process on the Request for Proposal for the Rewrite of the 2028 Bristol Plan of 
Conservation and Development filed with the Purchasing Dept.  
 
b. Subdivision Status Report - August 2026 
 
The City Planner explained there were no recent updates to the Subdivision Status report except for a couple months 
ago for the extension of the Blossom Estates to 2031. Staff noted a few months ago some bonds were renewed to 
2027.  
 
Commissioner Soares announced this was his last meeting with the Commission. The member expressed his 
thankfulness for the education he received on the many changes to the Regulations throughout the years. 
 
 
11.  Communications 
 
12.  Adjournment 
 
Chairman Veits designated himself, Regular Commissioners Pose, Soares and Nardi with Alternate Commissioner 
Klimek to vote on the adjournment. 
 
Motion was made by Commissioner Klimek to adjourn. 
Motion seconded by Commissioner Pose. 
Motion carried 5-0.
Bristol Planning Commission Regular Meeting of August 24, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 8 – 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:20 P.M. 
 
These minutes represent the proceedings of the meeting. 
This meeting was recorded. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Nancy King 
 
 
 
William Veits 
Chairman 
City Planning Commission
